official.deadline_note: JASSO publishes no application deadline of its own; the official page states 'Please ask the staff at the educational institution in which you are enrolled.' Each institution runs its own internal selection, so the operative deadline is the one your own school's international students' office sets.
official.application_cycle: Institutional nomination round (12-month period April-March, or 6-month period October-March); the currently advertised reservation round is the EJU 2nd Session in November 2026, with a parallel reservation route by Pre-arrival Admission for academic year 2026 spring and autumn enrolment
official.status_note: JASSO states 'There are no such universities or Japanese language institutes suspended application of this scholarship at present,' i.e. no listed institution has paused the scheme. JASSO published 2026 selection results (Japanese only) in June 2026 and continues to run the annual EJU-based reservation rounds.
official.tuition_coverage_note: JASSO publishes only a 'Monthly stipend' and no statement about tuition or enrolment fees; the financial condition refers to 'Allowance (excluding enrollment fee, tuition fee, etc.) received by the candidate must not exceed an average of 90,000 yen per month.'

Scholarship period of 12 months (April to the following March) or 6 months (October to the following March)

eligibility: Privately financed, i.e. not a grantee of the Japanese Government (Monbukagakusho/MEXT) Scholarship or any foreign government scholarship
Must hold the residence status of 'Student'

Enrolled as a full-time student at a graduate school (or holds at least an undergraduate degree and is enrolled as a research student at graduate level), an undergraduate school, a junior college, a college of technology (3rd year or above), a specialized course in a specialized training college, a preparatory Japanese language programme, a university preparatory course, or a Japanese language institute
Must meet the grading criteria specified in the application guidelines

Evidence of enrolment as a full-time student and grades for the grading criteria, submitted through the institution
Reservation Notice downloaded from 'My Page' on EJU Online (reservation holders only), copy submitted to the school of enrolment
Monthly signature sheet designated by JASSO, signed at the international students' office for the whole scholarship period

Monthly stipend of JPY 30,000 per month at Japanese language institutes

Pre-arrival admission reservation route: apply to the school you plan to enrol in, which nominates you before arrival
official.application_route: Apply through the educational institution you are enrolled at (or plan to enrol in) - JASSO does not accept applications directly from students; the EJU and pre-arrival reservation routes are handled by the school.
official.citizenship_residency: No nationality restriction is published; the candidate must be a privately-financed international student holding the residence status of 'Student' and be excluded if a Japanese Government (MEXT) or foreign government scholarship holder.
official.international_eligibility: Yes - open to privately-financed international students of any nationality who hold Student residence status
official.duration: 12 months (April to the following March) or 6 months (October to the following March); under the EJU reservation route, 12 months from April 2027 to March 2028 for enrolment between November 2026 and April 2027, or 6 months from October 2027 to March 2028 for enrolment between May 2027 and October 2027, with possible extension until course completion
official.description: JASSO describes this as a scholarship programme for privately-financed international students with excellent academic and character records who are enrolled in undergraduate schools, graduate schools, junior colleges, colleges of technology, specialized courses in specialized training colleges, university preparatory courses or Japanese language institutes in Japan and are facing financial difficulties. The number of students an educational institution can recommend depends on the number of international students enrolled in it.
official.program_type: Privately-financed international student honors scholarship, nominated by the host educational institution
official.english_requirement: Either CEFR B2 or above in English, JLPT N2 or above, EJU Japanese as a Foreign Language 200 points or more, or a language level separately recognised by JASSO. The language condition is waived for students of preparatory Japanese language programmes, university preparatory courses and Japanese language institutes.

verification.notes: Amounts, period, eligibility conditions, language condition and application route were read directly from JASSO's own English pages (about, pre-arrival admission reservation programme, and the EJU 2nd Session November 2026 reservation round). No deadline exists on the awarding body's side because nomination is institutional.

applicant_utility.summary: This stipend cannot be applied for directly - your enrolled (or soon-to-be-enrolled) Japanese school is the gatekeeper, and whether you can apply at all depends on how many international students that school has on its rolls. Budget your expectations around roughly 48,000 yen a month at undergraduate or graduate level, or 30,000 yen a month if you are at a Japanese language institute, for either 12 or 6 months. The financial test is stricter than most applicants expect: any allowance you already receive, excluding admission and tuition fees, must average no more than 90,000 yen per month, and a financial supporter living in Japan must earn under 5 million yen a year. You also take on an ongoing obligation - visiting the international students' office every single month to sign the JASSO sheet - so plan to stay enrolled and in 'Student' status throughout.
applicant_utility.best_fit: A financially stretched privately-financed international student already enrolled full-time in Japan who has a strong academic record and a language score of JLPT N2, EJU Japanese 200+, or CEFR B2.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm with your school's international students' office that it nominates candidates for this scholarship and ask for its internal cut-off date, which will be well before any JASSO date
Total up every allowance you currently receive, excluding admission and tuition fees, and confirm the monthly average stays at or under 90,000 yen
Check the income of any financial supporter resident in Japan against the 5 million yen per year ceiling before you apply

Certify your language level - JLPT N2, EJU Japanese 200+ or CEFR B2 - unless you are on a preparatory programme, university preparatory course or language institute course where the condition is waived
Read the Japanese-language application guidelines your school supplies, because the grading criteria that decide the award live only in that document
Diarise the monthly signature visit to the international students' office for the whole scholarship period, and agree to the JASSO career path survey
common_rejection_risks: Your institution has no nomination quota to spare - allocation scales with the number of international students enrolled, so some schools simply cannot put anyone forward
Exceeding the 90,000 yen monthly allowance ceiling because a small private transfer or part-time income was counted as support
A financial supporter living in Japan whose annual income sits at or above 5 million yen
Holding MEXT, another foreign government scholarship, or any scholarship whose rules forbid stacking it with an Honors Scholarship
Receiving JASSO Student Exchange Support Program support at the same time, which is expressly excluded
Losing the 'Student' residence status, transferring, withdrawing, or letting academic standing slip - JASSO can terminate disbursements for all of these
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Tuition, admission and other fees are entirely outside this stipend, and JASSO publishes no travel, installation or insurance component, so first-year costs such as the admission fee, tuition, flights, housing deposits and furnishing have to be found elsewhere.
document_audit: The detailed application guidelines are Japanese-only, so build in time to have a Japanese-speaking staff member or friend walk you through the grading criteria
The 90,000 yen allowance test is calculated as a monthly average excluding admission and tuition fees - gather bank statements and any remittance records before you are asked
A supporter's income evidence is needed whenever the supporter is resident in Japan, even if the money comes from abroad
Reservation holders must keep the Reservation Notice downloaded from EJU Online 'My Page' and hand a copy to the school of enrolment - it is not reissued on demand
Grading evidence is institution-issued, so the transcript format your school gives you may need to be re-requested in an admissible form
alerts: Nothing is on a published calendar: if you wait for a JASSO announcement you will miss your school's internal selection entirely
The stipend amount is explicitly 'subject to change each academic year' on the reservation pages, so do not build a 12-month budget on 48,000 yen without a buffer
Reservation holders who fail to enrol in the permitted institution types inside the stated window have their reservation cancelled outright
Keeping the award depends on a visible attendance record, not just on passing grades
Do not let this stipend overlap with the Student Exchange Support Program - that combination disqualifies you
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: You register interest with your institution (or with the school you plan to enrol in), the institution screens and nominates you to JASSO, and JASSO approves and pays the stipend through the school's international students' office.

official.deadline_note: FY2027 1st round deadline of 28 August 2026 (5 p.m. JST) has already passed; the next still-applicable round is the 2nd round at 23 April 2027 (5 p.m. JST). Both are deadlines for the host institution to transmit to JSPS, and host institutions may set their own deadline more than one month earlier.
official.status_note: JSPS's FY2027 application schedule still lists the 2nd round (application deadline 23 April 2027 by 5 p.m. JST, results early August 2027, arrival 1 September - 30 November 2027, approximately 120 fellowships). The 1st round closed on 28 August 2026.
official.tuition_coverage_note: No tuition is payable under this fellowship and JSPS publishes no tuition coverage; support is a maintenance allowance, airfare and miscellaneous items.
benefits: Maintenance allowance of JPY 362,000 per month
Round-trip air ticket, economy class, based on JSPS's regulations
A Grant-in-Aid for Scientific Research (Grant-in-Aid for JSPS Research Fellows) available to cover cooperative research-related expenses, applied for by the host researcher through their institution
eligibility: Be a citizen of a country that has diplomatic relations with Japan (JSPS treats Taiwanese and Palestinian researchers in this manner)

As of April 1, 2027, have obtained a doctoral degree within six years of the date the fellowship goes into effect (on or after 2 April 2021), or be expected to receive a Ph.D. by the start date of the fellowship period
Being employed, or not employed, in a full-time position is not considered

Japanese citizens and foreigners permitted permanent residence in Japan are not eligible; foreigners who obtained a doctoral degree from a Japanese university or who reside in Japan with a Residence Card are eligible
Those who have previously been awarded and started a fellowship under the JSPS Postdoctoral Fellowship for Research in Japan (Standard or Pathway to University positions in Japan) are not eligible

The applicant must be a host researcher at a KAKENHI-eligible research institution, be a full-time researcher (or judged able to execute the responsibility by the host institution), and wish to host an overseas researcher
Researchers who obtained their PhD within six years minus time taken for maternity and/or parental leave are eligible, with every four weeks of leave counted as one month
requirements: Applications must be submitted to JSPS by a host researcher in Japan via the head of their university or institution; candidates cannot apply directly
Applications must reach JSPS through the JSPS Electronic Application System by 5 p.m. JST on the round's deadline
The JSPS Electronic Application System opens approximately two months before the JSPS application deadlines
The candidate and host must have established contact in advance and created a concrete research plan
A selected fellow must submit the diploma or doctoral degree certificate so that it arrives at JSPS before the fellowship start date
As a rule, candidates are to stay in Japan continuously during the fellowship, concentrating on their research and not engaging in other work
Host researchers may submit up to three applications per recruitment; a fellow's tenure may start anytime within the published arrival window
Applicant and candidate must submit a research report using the separately prescribed formats before the JSPS deadline, and acknowledge the JSPS fellowship when publishing results
documents: Form 1, entered on the JSPS Electronic Application System by the host researcher (name, affiliated organisation, research theme, fellowship tenure, purpose and significance of collaboration, framework for hosting the invitee)
Form 2, prepared by the candidate and uploaded as Word or PDF (curriculum vitae, research achievements and results, research plan, academic goals after the fellowship ends, career plans)

Letter of Recommendation, one page, written and signed by the candidate's doctoral supervisor or another person other than the host researcher; a signature typed in a handwriting-style font is not accepted
Diploma or doctoral degree certificate, submitted to JSPS before the fellowship start date (not required at application)
For the parental/maternity leave adjustment, separate submission documents as directed by JSPS through the host institution
Japanese or English translations of any document whose original is in neither language
selection_criteria: Document review by six examiners per application on a 1-5 graduated scale, considering research achievements, the research plan, estimated research capacity, future potential of the research and establishment of new research networks
Panel review based on document review scores, selecting a specified number of applicants in each panel review section
That the collaboration will contribute to advancing science in Japan and other countries
That the collaboration can be expected to advance both the candidate's and the applicant's research work
That the applicant and candidate have established contact in advance and created a concrete research plan
That the applicant's institution has established a suitable place for the candidate to work and stay
That unbalance is avoided, as much as possible, in the selectees' nationalities, host institutions and areas of specialisation
That not only the document review score but also the examiners' reasons and comments are given adequate consideration
coverage: Maintenance allowance of JPY 362,000 per month
Round-trip air ticket (economy class) based on JSPS's regulations
JSPS states these amounts are subject to change for budgetary reasons
application_method: Host researcher logs in to the JSPS Electronic Application System, enters Form 1 and uploads Form 2 and the Letter of Recommendation, then transmits to the host institution by the institution's own deadline
Host institution verifies the content, confirms head-of-institution approval, checks the 'List of Candidates', then transmits to the President of JSPS by the JSPS deadline

Nomination channel: an overseas nominating authority may alternatively nominate a candidate; a duplicate application through both channels must be withdrawn once one acceptance notification is received
official.application_route: The Japanese host researcher applies on your behalf through the JSPS Electronic Application System, transmitting via the host institution to JSPS by 5 p.m. JST on the round deadline; you never submit directly.
official.study_mode: Full-time research residency in Japan for the whole fellowship period
official.citizenship_residency: Citizens of countries with diplomatic relations with Japan, including Taiwanese and Palestinian researchers; Japanese citizens and foreigners with permanent residence status in Japan are not eligible
official.international_eligibility: Yes - designed specifically for postdoctoral researchers from countries other than Japan; foreigners with a Residence Card in Japan or a doctorate from a Japanese university remain eligible
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: All fields of the humanities, social sciences and natural sciences are open; the host researcher selects the review category from the Review Section Table and Review Section Set
official.research_requirement: A concrete research plan for cooperative research with the Japanese host researcher is required, submitted as part of Form 2; the applicant and candidate are expected to have established contact in advance
official.duration: 12 to 24 months, provided in full month units; the period runs from the day the fellow arrives at an airport in Japan to the day they depart, and may not be divided into multiple stays
official.description: JSPS describes the Standard programme as providing an opportunity for excellent postdoctoral researchers from other countries to conduct cooperative research under the guidance of their hosts in universities and other research institutions in Japan, with selection run through two channels, open calls and nominations. All fields of the humanities, social sciences and natural sciences are open, and each open-call round awards approximately 120 fellowships.
official.program_type: Postdoctoral research fellowship - Standard programme, open call

not_confirmed: english_requirement - JSPS publishes no IELTS/TOEFL/JLPT score requirement for this programme; the FY2027 guidelines state only that application forms may be filled out in either English or Japanese unless otherwise instructed, and the FAQ confirms 'the application should be completed in either Japanese or English'
tuition_coverage - not applicable to a non-degree research fellowship and not stated as a benefit by JSPS
verification.notes: The JPY 362,000 monthly maintenance allowance, JPY 200,000 settling-in allowance, round-trip air ticket and overseas travel insurance, the 12-24 month duration and the candidate and host eligibility rules were read from JSPS's own 'About the Program (Standard)' page and the FY2027 application guideline PDF. Deadlines (1st round 28 August 2026, 2nd round 23 April 2027, both 5 p.m. JST), arrival windows, result publication periods and the 120 fellowships per round were read from the JSPS 'Application Schedule (Open Call)' page. The FY2027 application guideline PDF was downloaded from jsps.go.jp and its text parsed locally.

applicant_utility.summary: You cannot apply for this yourself - the whole application is lodged by a Japanese host researcher through the JSPS Electronic Application System, so your first task is finding and convincing a host, not filling in a form. Support is a monthly maintenance allowance of JPY 362,000 for 12 to 24 months plus a round-trip economy air ticket, a JPY 200,000 settling-in allowance and overseas travel insurance, and JSPS notes these figures can change for budgetary reasons. The tight eligibility constraint is the six-year clock measured from 1 April 2027: you need a doctorate awarded on or after 2 April 2021, or a Ph.D. expected by the fellowship start date, and any previous JSPS Postdoctoral (Standard or Pathway) fellowship permanently disqualifies you. Watch the two-round rhythm - the 1st round closed on 28 August 2026, so the live target is the 2nd round, which must reach JSPS by 5 p.m. JST on 23 April 2027.
applicant_utility.best_fit: An early-career postdoc within six years of their Ph.D. who already has, or can quickly build, a concrete joint research plan with a Japanese host researcher.
application_readiness_checklist: Secure a host researcher at a KAKENHI-eligible institution who agrees to apply on your behalf, and confirm they are a full-time researcher (or that their institution will vouch for their capacity)
Agree the research plan and fellowship tenure with the host in writing before the system opens, since JSPS screens explicitly for prior contact and a concrete plan
Ask the host institution's research administration office for its internal transmission deadline, which JSPS warns can be more than one month before the JSPS date
Count your years since the doctorate against the 2 April 2021 cut-off, and add any maternity or parental leave months back into the calculation
Have your doctoral supervisor (or another person who is not the host) sign a one-page Letter of Recommendation - typed handwriting-style fonts are rejected
Prepare Form 2 as a Word or PDF upload covering CV, research achievements, research plan, post-fellowship academic goals and career plans
Line up your diploma or doctoral degree certificate so it physically reaches JSPS before the fellowship start date
common_rejection_risks: No host, or a host at an institution that is not KAKENHI-eligible, since the application is lodged on the host's credentials
A doctoral degree outside the six-year window as of 1 April 2027, without documented maternity or parental leave to offset it
A prior JSPS Postdoctoral Standard or Pathway fellowship, which is an absolute bar
Host researcher retiring during the fellowship tenure, which JSPS says should stop the application being submitted at all
Thin evidence of prior contact between host and candidate - 'advancing science in Japan and other countries' and a concrete joint plan are explicit screening criteria
Sending the application through both the open call and an overseas nominating authority and failing to withdraw the losing duplicate
Missing the institution's internal deadline rather than the JSPS one, which is the most common way an otherwise strong file dies
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Accommodation beyond what the maintenance allowance covers, visas and residence-card fees, relocation within Japan, and any research expenses beyond what the optional Grant-in-Aid for JSPS Research Fellows covers; the airfare is only the round-trip ticket booked under JSPS's rules.
document_audit: The Letter of Recommendation must come from someone other than the host researcher and must be one page with a genuine signature or a self-signed electronic image
Form 2 and the Letter of Recommendation must be uploaded as PDF or Word, so keep editable copies until the system accepts them
Any document not originally in Japanese or English needs a Japanese or English translation attached
The doctoral degree certificate is not needed at application but must arrive at JSPS before the start date, and its absence cancels the fellowship
Leave-based eligibility extensions require separate submission documents arranged in advance through the host institution, not added later
The host must verify the 'List of Candidates' on the system before transmitting, so build time for that institutional check
alerts: A host institution's internal deadline can fall more than a month before the JSPS deadline of 23 April 2027, so treat early 2027 as the real working deadline
If you already live in Japan and have a mailing address before the start date, JSPS pays neither the outbound airfare nor the settling-in allowance
Fellowship periods run in full month units from airport arrival to airport departure and cannot be split into multiple stays
You must reside in Japan continuously and not take other employment; only research-related teaching, closely related projects, outreach and JSPS events are permitted with host approval
Duplicating an application across the open call and a nominating authority requires withdrawing one channel as soon as an acceptance notification arrives
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Candidate sends Form 2 and the recommendation letter to the host researcher, who enters Form 1 and uploads them on the JSPS Electronic Application System, transmits to the host institution, which verifies and sends it to the President of JSPS by 5 p.m. JST on the round deadline.
